caveats: Scores count AOI pixels classified in both years (valid, and in the training labels' radar regime in both), in every zone the AOI touches; with Hansen, only pixels Hansen maps as land (datamask 1).
Hansen Global Forest Change is itself a model, at 30 m, resampled here to the 10 m grid by nearest neighbour, so disagreement along patch edges is expected.

Hansen loss records stand-replacing tree cover loss of any cause, including fire, storms and selective or salvage logging followed by regrowth, while a conversion here needs a non-forest classification in year_b: loss that still reads as forest in year_b is a miss by construction, and regrowth after early loss in the window can hide it.

The headline reference is Hansen loss after 2019 through 2022 (lossyear codes 20 to 22), as survey S13 specifies. Annual embeddings and Hansen's detection year need not line up: loss Hansen dates to 2019 may already read as cleared in the 2019 embedding, and loss it dates to 2022 may still read as forest in the 2022 embedding. In this run the app converted 1.4% of Hansen 2019 loss pixels and 73.1% of Hansen 2022 loss pixels. Here the headline window scores higher (IoU 0.657 against 0.384). conversion_lag_aligned scores the same conversion against loss in 2019 through 2021 (codes 19 to 21) and loss_year_breakdown gives the share converted for every loss year. The brief's comparison with loss in 2022 alone (conversion_year_b_only) counts conversions in the earlier years of the window as false positives, so its precision is lower by construction.

The forest map agreement compares each year's forest map with Hansen's forest proxy for that year (treecover2000 at or above the forest cover cut and no loss by that year), over the pixels classified that year. Tree cover is not forest, pixels between the label cover cuts count as non-forest in the proxy, and the proxy cannot see forest that grew after 2000. The year_b agreement checks how the year_a classifier transfers: a low year_b score with a good year_a score means the year_b forest baseline is off.

An annual embedding sums the whole year, while Hansen dates loss to the year it was detected: forest cleared late in year_b can still read as forest in the year_b embedding (missed), and forest cleared in year_a can still read as forest in the year_a embedding (a conversion that Hansen dates outside the window). loss_year_breakdown gives, for each Hansen loss year, the share of its scored pixels the app converted, the share the classifier flipped from forest to non-forest before the cross-check and the cleaning, and the share of flips the cross-check cut removed (below_cut_share).

The cross-check cut is the stable_percentile percentile of the distance among AOI pixels classed forest in both years (survey N13). That set also holds real conversions the classifier still calls forest in year_b (partial or edge pixels, degradation, clearing late in year_b), so where much of the AOI changed the cut can rise into the change population and remove true conversions: cross_check_removed counts the classifier flips the cut removed by Hansen loss.
Reference: Hansen Global Forest Change GFC-2025-v1.13, tiles from https://storage.googleapis.com/earthenginepartners-hansen/{version}/Hansen_{version}_{layer}_{tile}.tif.

The classifier's labels came from Hansen (treecover2000 and lossyear), so agreement with Hansen is not independent of the reference. They were sampled outside the AOI only, in a ring 0 to 5 km from it, so the comparison inside the AOI is spatially held out.
